**Test image analysis:**
- Single tomato plant on yellow stakes
- Severe whole-plant collapse — leaves completely brown and hanging downward
- Progressive death from bottom to top (lower portions completely dead, some green at the very top)
- Black plastic mulch visible on ground
- Adjacent plants appear healthy/unaffected

**Comparison summary:**
- **Bacterial_Wilt**: Shows complete, sudden whole-plant collapse with drooping dead leaves — strong visual match
- **Bacterial_Canker_And_Wilt_Of_Tomato**: Reference image 1573932 shows dead, dried plants hanging on stakes — also very strong match; the progressive bottom-to-top pattern fits canker wilt
- **Verticillium_Wilt**: Less severe wilt, more yellowing, V-shaped lesions — less matching
- **Southern_Bacterial_Wilt**: Shows root rot and field wilting but less complete collapse
- **Late_Blight**: Dark/blackened tissue, not dry brown wilt
- All other classes (leaf spots, mold, virus, etc.): Not matching the whole-plant wilt pattern

**Decision:** The test image shows a progressive wilt pattern from bottom to top with dried, hanging brown leaves — more consistent with Bacterial_Canker_And_Wilt_Of_Tomato than the sudden uniform wilt of Bacterial_Wilt. The Bacterial_Canker reference (image 1573932) shows nearly identical dead, shriveled plants on stakes matching the staking setup and overall death pattern in the test image.
